our_text: Local history states timber harvested in the surrounding area was loaded from the bluffs onto doghole schooners for San Francisco
source: Ocean Cove Campground & Store, 'History of Ocean Cove', https://www.oceancove.org/?page_id=219 (fetched via Wayback; source reads 'Timber was harvested in the surrounding area, then loaded from the bluffs onto "Dog Hole" schooners, and sent to San Francisco' — our sentence is the source's with only three function words changed; it evaded the n-gram scan)
fix: The Ocean Cove local history states: 'Timber was harvested in the surrounding area, then loaded from the bluffs onto "Dog Hole" schooners, and sent to San Francisco'

our_text: John and Andrew Fisk built the first landing in 1867

fix: The Fisk brothers, John and Andrew, opened the first landing here in 1867

our_text: H.A. Richardson bought the property in 1881, built his own chute

our_text: steam- and horse-drawn railroads to the cliff edge, and their own fleet of schooners and steam schooners
source: NOAA GFNMS, doghole_stewartspoint.html ('a system of steam and horse drawn railroads to move the forest products to the cliff edge. The Richardson's even owned their own fleet of schooners and steam schooners')
fix: rail lines, steam- and horse-powered, running out to the bluff edge, and a family fleet of sailing schooners and steam schooners

our_text: until trucks replaced water shipment in 1925
source: NOAA GFNMS, doghole_stewartspoint.html ('continued on for 40 years until trucks replaced water shipment in 1925')

our_text: survives as an essentially unaltered doghole-port hamlet

our_text: system of steam and horse-drawn railroads from mills to cliff edge

our_text: the mill burned in 1910 and the wire chute was likely abandoned soon after

our_text: brothers William and George Bender built a mill and wire chute just south

our_text: the first such apparatus in the area

our_text: ownership passed to Frederick M. Helmke in 1865, who closed the mill in 1876

our_text: the chute stayed active under the Kruse family, transhipping for other mills including Platt's mill

our_text: It had its own wharf and a railroad, and the town a large hotel; the mill burned and was never rebuilt

our_text: by 1875 Bihler and D.L.B. Ross built a landing with a slide chute, adding a second in 1876

fix: Bihler and D.L.B. Ross had a landing and slide chute working by 1875, with a second chute following in 1876

our_text: had over a dozen buildings (hotel, store, post office, blacksmith, wagon shop, livery)

our_text: shipping six-foot railroad ties to San Pedro for the Los Angeles Railway

our_text: the cable was taken down in 1884 and the business moved to Russian Gulch Landing
